html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. AI: artificial intelligence

  • A time plan for 60 items in 120 minutes
  • A method to read an item, spot the binding concern and eliminate distractors
  • How to handle multiple-response items
  • Policies and logistics on exam day
  • A final review checklist and a plan for the last week

2Time Plan

  • 60 items in 120 minutes is 2 minutes per item, which is generous: you can read carefully.
  • First pass (about 80 minutes): answer what you know in about 80 seconds, mark the rest and move on.
  • Second pass (about 30 minutes): work the marked items with a fresh mind.
  • Last 10 minutes: check that multiple-response items have the right number of answers and that nothing is blank.
  • Never leave an item blank; make your best choice. Do not spend more than about 3 minutes on one item at the first pass.
  • There is no domain pass mark; only the total scaled score (720) counts.
Exam tip

Calm and steady beats fast. With two minutes per item, the usual errors come from misreading the question, not from running out of time.

3Reading an Item

  1. Read the last sentence first ("What is the most appropriate action?") and note how many answers to select.
  2. Read the scenario for the binding concern: accuracy, data sensitivity, cost or speed, context length, who is accountable, which feature fits.
  3. Predict the answer before you read the options.
  4. Compare the options with your prediction and the ten decision rules (Module 0).
Word in the stem Points to...
"confident", "cites a section", "before sending" Verify against the authoritative source
"vague", "generic", "too long" Improve the prompt (context, format, constraints)
"large project", "multiple parts" Decompose into reviewed steps
"current", "today's price" Web search
"comprehensive", "multi-source", "report with citations" Research
"complex reasoning", "logic error" Extended thinking (with verification)
"high volume", "fast", "low cost" Lighter model, lower effort
"same background every time" Project
"repeatable procedure" Skill
"latest Drive files", "email" Connector (within permissions, approvals)
"customer names", "account numbers", "health", "policy restricts" Remove or anonymize; approved tool; policy
"hiring", "credit", "benefits", "legal advice" Qualified human decides; disclose
"drifted", "very long chat" Summarize and restart
"not working" Diagnose and change one thing
"API", "integrate", "automate with code" Escalate
Exam tip

The cause or the constraint is usually in the stem. Use it before looking at the options.

4Eliminating Distractors

Cross out options that:

  • Trust without verifying ("send it because it sounds sure")
  • Use self-assessment as validation ("ask Claude if it is sure")
  • Go to an extreme ("always", "never", "only") without reason
  • Skip the human where stakes are high
  • Share sensitive data against policy, or rely on "don't retain" as protection
  • Over-tool (Research for a one-line fact) or under-tool (chat for a multi-source report)
  • Redo everything when one change would do
  • Improvise technical integration instead of escalating
  • Hide or fake (AI use, reviews, sources)

Then pick the option that verifies, protects data, fits the task and keeps a person accountable.

Exam tip

Change an answer only when you can name the rule it breaks

Multiple-response items

  • The stem says exactly how many to choose ("Select TWO"). Choose that number.
  • Judge each option on its own: is it true and does it answer the question?
  • Do not assume the two answers are related; sometimes they are separate good practices.
  • If you are stuck, eliminate the clearly wrong options first.

5Policies and Logistics

Topic What to know
Registration Through the Anthropic Partner Academy and Pearson VUE; online proctored or test center
Reschedule or cancel Up to 24 hours before; later changes forfeit the fee
ID Valid, unexpired government photo ID; the name must match the registration exactly
Accommodations Request and get approval from Pearson VUE before scheduling
Agreements You accept a confidentiality and non-disclosure agreement; never share exam content
Conduct Stay in view of the webcam if online; clear desk; no phones, watches, headphones or notes; no communication
Retakes 14 / 30 / 90 days; max 4 attempts per rolling 12 months; fee per attempt
Result Pass or fail and scaled score, plus percent correct per domain
Validity and renewal 12 months; on-time renewal is a free, non-proctored assessment; a lapsed credential needs the full exam again
Appeals Within 14 days through Pearson VUE support; scoring standard and individual items are not appealable

[Verify live] The guide is version 1.0 (July 2026). Check the Partner Academy for the current guide, fee and rules before you book.

6Final Review Checklist

  • I can state the ten decision rules without looking.
  • I can build a strong prompt and decompose a complex request.
  • I know the error types (hallucination, wrong numbers, outdated, overstated abilities, bias) and the checks that catch them.
  • I know when a qualified human must review.
  • I can choose between web search, thinking and Research, and between Haiku, Sonnet and Opus style models.
  • I can decide to restart, summarize or persist.
  • I can configure a Project (instructions and knowledge), and I know connectors, Skills and memory.
  • I can classify data sensitivity and name the safe action.
  • I know the main points of AI policy, governance and ethics.
  • I can diagnose a weak output and optimize a workflow.
  • I know what to escalate and how to brief a Developer.
  • I have used Claude to build a Project and evaluated its outputs for accuracy and bias.

The last week

  • Seven to four days before: reread the notes of the heaviest domains (Output Evaluation, then Workflow and Solution Design, then Governance and Prompting), redo their scenario questions, and write down every miss with the reason.
  • Three days before: walk through the decision chooser in Module 17 aloud; reread the names and values table.
  • The day before: light review only: the ten decision rules and the time plan. Check your ID, registration name and test setup, and sleep.
  • On the day: arrive or log in early, read each item's last sentence first, and keep to the time plan.
